subject: Post-call recap & POC charter — Veridian AI
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@veridian.ai>; eng-ops@veridian.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed POC charter (next steps)

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: your ingestion pipeline is inconsistent, high latency for batch scoring, and you’re seeing token-level cost spikes with peak traffic.
- Goal: reduce inference latency for interactive analyst queries to <500ms median and reduce per-request token cost by ~30% for the batch scoring job.

Proposed POC scope (2-week initial sprint)
1) Scope: deploy Redwood Dedicated trial instance behind Veridian VPC for a single model (open-llama-13b variant), run two workloads:
   - Interactive query path (50–200 tokens) — measure p50/p95 latency and quality on a 200-example prompt set.
   - Nightly batch scoring (avg 25k items/day) — measure throughput, per-token cost, and end-to-end run time.
2) Success metrics: p50 latency < 500ms for interactive; p95 < 1s for 90% of queries; batch throughput improvement 2x and 30% lower cost per item.
3) Owners: Veridian Eng Ops for data & access (Samir + eng-ops), Redwood: Ava (POC lead) + Karthik (runtime tuning). Monica covering prompt evals.
4) Data & access required: S3 read-only bucket with sample batch (25k items), a subset of interactive prompt logs, and ability to run a test harness behind your VPC.
5) Eval plan: we’ll run a prompt set (attached) of 200 labeled examples and an automated scoring job that compares model outputs to your rubric. Monica will share the eval template.

Attachments: VID-8721_POC_scope_v1.pdf (summary & checklist), access-checklist.txt

Immediate next steps
- Samir/Eng Ops: confirm access window and send IAM role (read-only) by 2026-07-09 EOD.
- Ava/Karthik: finalize Dedicated config (GPU type, batch window) & share an infra runbook by 2026-07-08.
- Monica: share prompt eval template and baseline scoring script.

If that matches what you heard, I’ll queue a calendar invite for an ops kickoff (30 min) and open the HubSpot MAM for tracking.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@veridian.ai>

Cc: eng-ops@veridian.ai; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC charter (next steps)

Ava — thanks for the crisp recap. This is exactly what we need. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Model: we’d like to try the open-llama-13b quantized variant but also want a fallback to a 7B distilled variant if latency/p95 doesn’t meet expectations. Is that possible within the trial?
2) Data: the sample batch is ready (s3://veridian-prod/poc-samples/vid-8721/), but it contains PII in two fields — we’ll provide a redacted/hashed version for the POC and a small non-PII set for the interactive tests.
3) Timeline: we can confirm IAM role on 7/9 morning PST, but our security review will only allow non-production keys (short-lived) during the POC.

We’re good to proceed once you confirm the model fallback and the Dedicated config. Also please add a short note about rollback/failure modes in the runbook (what happens if p95 spikes).

—Samir
Head of Eng Ops, Veridian AI
samir.khan@veridian.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC charter (next steps)

Samir / Ava — quick technical confirmation from Redwood runtime side:

- Fallback approach: yes — we can configure a routing policy that attempts open-llama-13b quantized first and falls back to open-llama-7b-dist in under 50ms of routing decision time. Fallback will be metric-driven (p95 or queue length threshold).
- Dedicated config suggestion: 1 x A100-80GB for the 13B quantized variant (small pool), 1 x A10G for the 7B-dist fallback; enable continuous batching for batch scoring window and 2s interactive batching bucket.
- Rollback/failure: runbook will include automatic fallback to the smaller model if p95 > 1s for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows, and circuit-breaker to drop to a cached response if queue length exceeds threshold.

I’ll draft the infra section of the runbook and drop into the Drive folder by EOD Thu.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- Model plan: open-llama-13b-quantized primary; open-llama-7b-dist fallback as Karthik outlined.
- Data: use the redacted S3 path for the POC. We will only request short-lived credentials (as you noted).
- Rollback: automatic fallback & circuit-breaker will be included in the runbook.

Immediate actions
- Veridian (Samir/Eng Ops): share IAM role ARN + sample object path by 2026-07-09 17:00 PST.
- Redwood (Ava/Karthik): infra runbook + Dedicated config + short test-playbook by 2026-07-08 18:00 PST (Karthik to drop infra notes in Drive).
- Redwood (Monica): prompt eval suite + scoring script by 2026-07-09 morning.

I’ll send a 30-min kickoff invite for Mon, 2026-07-12 10:00 PST (ops + eng + security). If that time doesn’t work, let me know and I’ll propose alternatives.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll mark the MAM in HubSpot and attach the scope doc as VID-8721_POC_scope_v1.pdf.

Best,
Ava
